subsystems.name: Sorbent bed
subsystems.role: captures water vapour from air using a metal-organic framework.

subsystems.name: Air circulation
subsystems.role: moves ambient air through the sorbent bed.

subsystems.name: Desorption heater
subsystems.role: warms the sorbent to release captured water as vapour.

subsystems.name: Condenser
subsystems.role: cools the humid vapour so it condenses into liquid water.

subsystems.name: Water treatment
subsystems.role: makes the condensate safe and pleasant to drink.

subsystems.name: Control and power
subsystems.role: runs the adsorption-desorption cycles and manages energy.

buildSteps.title: Synthesize the MOF
buildSteps.detail: metal salts and organic linker molecules are dissolved, heated, and crystallised; the powder is washed and dried to leave a porous framework that traps water.

buildSteps.title: Shape the sorbent
buildSteps.detail: the MOF powder is coated onto metal fins or pressed into pellets to maximise surface area and air contact.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the sorbent bed
buildSteps.detail: coated fins or pellets are stacked in a housing with gaps for air to pass through.

buildSteps.title: Add air handling
buildSteps.detail: a fan, ducts, and seals are fitted so ambient air can be drawn across the sorbent during the night cycle.

buildSteps.title: Install the heater
buildSteps.detail: a solar absorber or resistive element is coupled to the bed to drive off water when heated.

buildSteps.title: Build the condenser
buildSteps.detail: a cooled coil and collection tray are connected to the desorbing vapour stream.

buildSteps.title: Add water treatment
buildSteps.detail: filters, a UV lamp, and a mineral cartridge are plumbed between the condenser and the storage tank.

buildSteps.title: Integrate controls and power
buildSteps.detail: sensors and a microcontroller are wired to switch between adsorption and desorption; a solar panel and battery provide off-grid power.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: the device is run at different humidities and temperatures to measure water yield and tune cycle times.

prerequisites.tech: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with high water uptake at low humidity
prerequisites.why: lab-scale MOFs can harvest water at low relative humidity, but manufacturing them at low cost and scale is still developing.
desorption needs heat, and solar collectors or waste heat are widely available.
dehumidifiers and water filters are mature technologies.
off-grid operation depends on efficient components.
producing tonnes of MOF per year with consistent quality is not yet routine.

pathway.milestone: pilot devices using MOFs produce water at rates measured in litres per day per kilogram of sorbent in arid conditions
pathway.unlocks: drinking water for remote households and emergency relief.

pathway.milestone: improved MOFs with higher capacity and faster cycling
pathway.unlocks: higher yield per unit mass, making devices smaller and cheaper.

pathway.milestone: integration with solar PV and thermal storage for round-the-clock operation
pathway.unlocks: reliable daily water supply independent of weather.

pathway.milestone: mass production and deployment in water-stressed regions
pathway.unlocks: community-scale atmospheric water harvesting as a complement to wells and desalination.
